styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall prop with a stone pedestal, iron post, gold bands, glass lantern and crown cap. Its measured 19 visible tones per full tile matches the richer references (well 20, cheese stall 17) and is well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills. The 53% near-neutral dark edge share is a mixed outline, close to the bench (44%) and well (33%) and far from the pure near-black crook lamp (100%). It has about 24 colours in total, so each material (stone, iron, gold, glass) gets roughly 3-4 steps against Beodeul's 5-6. The candidate's per-tile tone count and 0% flat coverage still show it carries as much visible information as the references. Judged by eye, it is not thinner or more sticker-like than the crook lamp reference and is richer than it. It is slightly shallower in ramp depth but acceptable next to the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The lamp is a thin, tall prop, so I judged mostly by eye against prop-lamp-crook and prop-well-roofed. The numbers look fine: 19 visible tones per tile (references 17 and 20), 0% near-flat coverage, no flat fills. Structure is good, with a stone pedestal, blue plaque, banded iron post, octagonal lit lantern and gold cap. But the whole piece uses only 24 distinct colours (well 38, stall 40), which suggests each material ramp is short. The pedestal stone, the iron post and the gold bands and cap each look like about 3-4 steps, against 5-6 on the Beodeul references. Dark edges are 53% near-neutral, which is mixed: part of the outline is a neutral dark line, not a clear dark tone of the neighbouring material as in the references. Texture is limited to a few dots on the stone, with little per-stone shading or grain on the post. Overall it reads cleaner and slightly more sticker-like than the references, so it falls just short, and when in doubt it fails.
